records.context: Annotation works on single-object extracted image regions. Producing them with Measure means running it over a whole laboratory microplate -- about twenty minutes for 52 microscope fields of view on a 30-core machine -- and running it again to cut the extracted image regions differently.
records.label: spacr.annotation_dataset#1

records.source: Annotation works on single-object crops. Producing them with Measure means running it over a whole plate -- about twenty minutes for 52 fields on a 30-core machine -- and running it again to cut the crops differently.
records.translation: La anotación trabaja con recortes de objetos individuales. Producirlos con Measure significa ejecutarlo sobre toda una placa -- unos veinte minutos para 52 campos en una máquina de 30 núcleos -- y volver a ejecutarlo para cortar los recortes de otra forma.

records.context: Every microscope field of view's objects are already described twice over once Measure has run: by the label masks inside the merged arrays, and by the coordinate columns in ``measurements.db``. Either is enough to cut extracted image regions from, so a second set can be built in seconds without measuring anything again.
records.label: spacr.annotation_dataset#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Every field's objects are already described twice over once Measure has run: by the label masks inside the merged arrays, and by the coordinate columns in ``measurements.db``. Either is enough to cut crops from, so a second set can be built in seconds without measuring anything again.
records.translation: Una vez ejecutado Measure, los objetos de cada campo ya están descritos dos veces: por las máscaras de etiquetas dentro de las matrices fusionadas y por las columnas de coordenadas de ``measurements.db``. Cualquiera de las dos basta para cortar recortes, de modo que un segundo conjunto puede construirse en segundos sin volver a medir nada.

records.context: ComBat estimates the batch effect from whatever variation is left after the design matrix has absorbed the biology. If the biology is not in that design, it is part of "whatever is left" and gets removed along with the plate effect. That failure is silent: the corrected table looks cleaner, the batch diagnostic improves, and the treatment effect is gone.
records.label: spacr.batch_correction.NO_COVARIATE#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ComBat estimates the batch effect from whatever variation is left after the design matrix has absorbed the biology. If the biology is not in that design, it is part of "whatever is left" and gets removed along with the plate effect. That failure is silent: the corrected table looks cleaner, the batch diagnostic improves, and the treatment effect is gone.
records.translation: ComBat estima el efecto de lote a partir de la variación que queda después de que la matriz de diseño haya absorbido la biología. Si la biología no está en ese diseño, forma parte de "whatever is left" (lo que queda) y se elimina junto con el efecto de placa. Ese fallo es silencioso: la tabla corregida parece más limpia, el diagnóstico de lotes mejora y el efecto del tratamiento ha desaparecido.

records.context: ``combat`` is the empirical-Bayes method of Johnson, Li & Rabinovich (2007). Unlike the four above it fits a *model*: every feature is regressed on batch indicators **and** on the biology named by ``covariate``, and only the batch part of that fit is removed. The per-batch location and scale are then shrunk toward the distribution of the same parameter across all features, which is what makes it usable on a laboratory microplate with few microplate sample positions where a per-feature estimate would be noise.
records.label: spacr.batch_correction.correct_batch_effects#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``combat`` is the empirical-Bayes method of Johnson, Li & Rabinovich (2007). Unlike the four above it fits a *model*: every feature is regressed on batch indicators **and** on the biology named by ``covariate``, and only the batch part of that fit is removed. The per-batch location and scale are then shrunk toward the distribution of the same parameter across all features, which is what makes it usable on a plate with few wells where a per-feature estimate would be noise.
records.translation: ``combat`` es el método bayesiano empírico de Johnson, Li & Rabinovich (2007). A diferencia de los cuatro anteriores, ajusta un *modelo*: cada característica se regresa sobre indicadores de lote **y** sobre la biología indicada en ``covariate``, y solo se elimina la parte del ajuste correspondiente al lote. Después, la posición y la escala por lote se contraen hacia la distribución del mismo parámetro en todas las características, que es lo que lo hace utilizable en una placa con pocos pocillos, donde una estimación por característica sería ruido.

records.context: That covariate is not optional and has no default. A batch effect estimated without it absorbs any contrast that happens to differ between plates -- which, in a screen where treatments are laid out plate by plate, is the treatment effect. The correction then reports a cleaner batch diagnostic and removes the treatment effect. Pass the biology to keep, or pass :data:`NO_COVARIATE` to record that there is none.
records.label: spacr.batch_correction.correct_batch_effects#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: That covariate is not optional and has no default. A batch effect estimated without it absorbs any contrast that happens to differ between plates -- which, in a screen where treatments are laid out plate by plate, is the treatment effect. The correction then reports a cleaner batch diagnostic and removes the treatment effect. Pass the biology to keep, or pass :data:`NO_COVARIATE` to record that there is none.
records.translation: Esa covariable no es opcional y no tiene valor predeterminado. Un efecto de lote estimado sin ella absorbe cualquier contraste que resulte diferir entre placas -- lo que, en un cribado en el que los tratamientos se distribuyen placa por placa, es el efecto del tratamiento. La corrección informa entonces de un diagnóstico de lotes más limpio y elimina el efecto del tratamiento. Pase la biología que se debe conservar, o pase :data:`NO_COVARIATE` para registrar que no hay ninguna.

records.context: The problem
records.label: spacr.illumination#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The problem
records.translation: El problema

records.context: *Why the surface fit on top.* Illumination is a physically smooth, low-frequency function of position: a lamp profile plus a vignette. Fitting a low-order 2-D polynomial (default degree 4, 15 terms) to the per-pixel median imposes exactly that prior, so residual object structure and photon noise cannot leak into the gain map and be baked into every measurement on the laboratory microplate. The fit is trimmed twice against a MAD threshold, so a persistent bright artefact -- a fluorescent speck in the same place on every microscope field of view -- is rejected rather than smeared into the surface. For illumination that is genuinely not polynomial (a dust shadow, a sharply structured lamp) pass ``estimator='smooth'``: the same per-pixel median, Gaussian-smoothed at 1/16 of the short side and interpolated back to full resolution.
records.label: spacr.illumination#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: *Why the surface fit on top.* Illumination is a physically smooth, low-frequency function of position: a lamp profile plus a vignette. Fitting a low-order 2-D polynomial (default degree 4, 15 terms) to the per-pixel median imposes exactly that prior, so residual object structure and photon noise cannot leak into the gain map and be baked into every measurement on the plate. The fit is trimmed twice against a MAD threshold, so a persistent bright artefact -- a fluorescent speck in the same place on every field -- is rejected rather than smeared into the surface. For illumination that is genuinely not polynomial (a dust shadow, a sharply structured lamp) pass ``estimator='smooth'``: the same per-pixel median, Gaussian-smoothed at 1/16 of the short side and interpolated back to full resolution.
records.translation: *Por qué el ajuste de superficie encima.* La iluminación es una función físicamente suave y de baja frecuencia de la posición: el perfil de una lámpara más un viñeteado. Ajustar un polinomio 2-D de orden bajo (por defecto de grado 4, 15 términos) a la mediana por píxel impone exactamente esa suposición previa, de modo que la estructura residual de los objetos y el ruido de fotones no pueden filtrarse al mapa de ganancia y quedar incorporados a todas las mediciones de la placa. El ajuste se recorta dos veces frente a un umbral de MAD, de modo que un artefacto brillante persistente -- una mota fluorescente en el mismo lugar de cada campo -- se rechaza en lugar de extenderse por la superficie. Para una iluminación que realmente no es polinómica (la sombra de una mota de polvo, una lámpara con estructura marcada), pase ``estimator='smooth'``: la misma mediana por píxel, suavizada con un filtro gaussiano a 1/16 del lado corto e interpolada de nuevo a resolución completa.

records.context: *Why not BaSiC.* BaSiC's low-rank + sparse decomposition is the better estimator when you have hundreds of microscope fields of view and a genuine dark-microscope field of view to recover, but it is an iterative optimisation with its own convergence failure modes, and its dark-microscope field of view term is only identifiable because of those extra assumptions. From a single acquisition, ``dark`` and ``flat`` are not separately identifiable at all: multiplying ``flat`` by a constant and absorbing it into the per-microscope field of view brightness leaves every observation unchanged. Estimating a dark-microscope field of view anyway -- for instance from the per-pixel minimum across microscope fields of view, which is the usual shortcut -- returns *dark plus the dimmest background*, and subtracting it removes real signal. ``dark`` is therefore not estimated: it is 0 unless you supply the camera offset you measured from a dark frame, via ``illumination_dark``.
records.label: spacr.illumination#11
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: *Why not BaSiC.* BaSiC's low-rank + sparse decomposition is the better estimator when you have hundreds of fields and a genuine dark-field to recover, but it is an iterative optimisation with its own convergence failure modes, and its dark-field term is only identifiable because of those extra assumptions. From a single acquisition, ``dark`` and ``flat`` are not separately identifiable at all: multiplying ``flat`` by a constant and absorbing it into the per-field brightness leaves every observation unchanged. Estimating a dark-field anyway -- for instance from the per-pixel minimum across fields, which is the usual shortcut -- returns *dark plus the dimmest background*, and subtracting it removes real signal. ``dark`` is therefore not estimated: it is 0 unless you supply the camera offset you measured from a dark frame, via ``illumination_dark``.
records.translation: *Por qué no BaSiC.* La descomposición de bajo rango + dispersa de BaSiC es el mejor estimador cuando se dispone de cientos de campos y de un campo oscuro real que recuperar, pero es una optimización iterativa con sus propios modos de fallo de convergencia, y su término de campo oscuro solo es identificable gracias a esas suposiciones adicionales. A partir de una sola adquisición, ``dark`` y ``flat`` no son identificables por separado en absoluto: multiplicar ``flat`` por una constante y absorberla en el brillo de cada campo deja todas las observaciones sin cambios. Estimar de todos modos un campo oscuro -- por ejemplo, a partir del mínimo por píxel entre campos, que es el atajo habitual -- devuelve *el oscuro más el fondo más tenue*, y restarlo elimina señal real. Por tanto, ``dark`` no se estima: vale 0 salvo que se proporcione mediante ``illumination_dark`` el desplazamiento de la cámara medido en un fotograma oscuro.

records.context: :func:`spacr.measure.measure_crop` measures fields in a :class:`multiprocessing.Pool`. Under ``spawn`` / ``forkserver`` each worker is a fresh interpreter with an empty hook registry, so a correction registered only in the parent is applied to no field, and the processing session completes without an error while every number is uncorrected. :func:`enable_illumination_correction` therefore does more than register the hook: it writes the model path to :data:`MODEL_ENV_VAR` and appends ``spacr.illumination:install`` to ``SPACR_MEASURE_HOOKS``, which every start method inherits, so each worker installs the correction for itself. :func:`worker_delivery_status` reports whether that is actually in place, and :func:`enable_illumination_correction` prints it.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :func:`spacr.measure.measure_crop` measures fields in a :class:`multiprocessing.Pool`. Under ``spawn`` / ``forkserver`` each worker is a fresh interpreter with an empty hook registry, so a correction registered only in the parent is applied to no field, and the run completes without an error while every number is uncorrected. :func:`enable_illumination_correction` therefore does more than register the hook: it writes the model path to :data:`MODEL_ENV_VAR` and appends ``spacr.illumination:install`` to ``SPACR_MEASURE_HOOKS``, which every start method inherits, so each worker installs the correction for itself. :func:`worker_delivery_status` reports whether that is actually in place, and :func:`enable_illumination_correction` prints it.
records.translation: :func:`spacr.measure.measure_crop` mide los campos en un :class:`multiprocessing.Pool`. Con ``spawn`` / ``forkserver``, cada worker es un intérprete nuevo con un registro de hooks vacío, de modo que una corrección registrada solo en el proceso padre no se aplica a ningún campo, y la ejecución termina sin errores mientras todos los números quedan sin corregir. Por eso :func:`enable_illumination_correction` hace algo más que registrar el hook: escribe la ruta del modelo en :data:`MODEL_ENV_VAR` y añade ``spacr.illumination:install`` a ``SPACR_MEASURE_HOOKS``, que heredan todos los métodos de inicio, de modo que cada worker instala la corrección por sí mismo. :func:`worker_delivery_status` indica si eso está realmente en marcha, y :func:`enable_illumination_correction` lo imprime.

records.context: No microscope lights a microscope field of view evenly. A lamp profile, vignetting in the objective, a tilted condenser and dirt on the optics together make the same cell measure brighter at the centre of the microscope field of view than at its edge -- routinely 10-40 % between the middle and a corner on a widefield screening experiment. Every intensity feature spaCR writes (``*_mean_intensity``, ``*_percentile_*``, the radial distribution, the texture image data channels that are computed on intensity) therefore carries a **position-dependent bias**, and because objects are not distributed identically over every microplate sample position, that bias does not average out: it survives into the per-microplate sample position aggregate, and from there into classification and regression as an effect that looks entirely real and is entirely an artefact of the optics.
records.label: spacr.illumination#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: No microscope lights a field of view evenly. A lamp profile, vignetting in the objective, a tilted condenser and dirt on the optics together make the same cell measure brighter at the centre of the field than at its edge -- routinely 10-40 % between the middle and a corner on a widefield screen. Every intensity feature spaCR writes (``*_mean_intensity``, ``*_percentile_*``, the radial distribution, the texture channels that are computed on intensity) therefore carries a **position-dependent bias**, and because objects are not distributed identically over every well, that bias does not average out: it survives into the per-well aggregate, and from there into classification and regression as an effect that looks entirely real and is entirely an artefact of the optics.
records.translation: Ningún microscopio ilumina un campo de visión de forma uniforme. El perfil de la lámpara, el viñeteado del objetivo, un condensador inclinado y la suciedad de la óptica hacen que la misma célula se mida más brillante en el centro del campo que en el borde -- habitualmente un 10-40 % entre el centro y una esquina en un cribado de campo amplio. Por tanto, cada característica de intensidad que escribe spaCR (``*_mean_intensity``, ``*_percentile_*``, la distribución radial y los canales de textura que se calculan sobre la intensidad) lleva un **sesgo dependiente de la posición**, y como los objetos no se distribuyen igual en todos los pocillos, ese sesgo no se compensa al promediar: sobrevive en el agregado por pocillo y, de ahí, pasa a la clasificación y a la regresión como un efecto que parece totalmente real y es totalmente un artefacto de la óptica.

records.context: It is also the root cause of the plate-scale edge effects :mod:`spacr.plate_qc` already detects and reports. That module reports them; this module removes the bias from the measured intensities.

records.context: *Why the median across microscope fields of view.* A pixel is covered by a cell in only a minority of the microscope fields of view on a laboratory microplate, so the across-microscope field of view median at that pixel sees background almost every time and the objects drop out. Each microscope field of view is first divided by its own median, so a densely-seeded microscope field of view does not pull the estimate up because it has more cells in it -- what is being averaged is the *relative* profile, not the brightness.

records.source: *Why the median across fields.* A pixel is covered by a cell in only a minority of the fields on a plate, so the across-field median at that pixel sees background almost every time and the objects drop out. Each field is first divided by its own median, so a densely-seeded field does not pull the estimate up because it has more cells in it -- what is being averaged is the *relative* profile, not the brightness.
records.translation: *Por qué la mediana entre campos.* Un píxel solo está cubierto por una célula en una minoría de los campos de una placa, así que la mediana entre campos en ese píxel ve fondo casi siempre y los objetos desaparecen. Cada campo se divide primero por su propia mediana, de modo que un campo sembrado densamente no eleva la estimación por tener más células -- lo que se promedia es el perfil *relativo*, no el brillo.

records.translation: Esta clase, y no la maquinaria de hooks, se encarga de la conversión de ida y vuelta del dtype (véase :func:`spacr.measure_hooks.apply_preprocessing_hooks`). Una entrada entera se corrige en float32 y se devuelve *redondeando al más cercano* y luego recortando al rango del dtype:

records.context: **round, not truncate.** Truncation would shave a mean of 0.5 counts off every corrected pixel. Averaged over a 500-pixel object that does not wash out -- it is a systematic, one-directional shift of exactly the kind this feature exists to remove. Rounding is unbiased.

records.source: **round, not truncate.** Truncation would shave a mean of 0.5 counts off every corrected pixel. Averaged over a 500-pixel object that does not wash out -- it is a systematic, one-directional shift of exactly the kind this feature exists to remove. Rounding is unbiased.
records.translation: **redondear, no truncar.** Truncar restaría una media de 0.5 cuentas a cada píxel corregido. Promediado sobre un objeto de 500 píxeles, eso no se diluye -- es un desplazamiento sistemático y en un solo sentido, exactamente del tipo que esta función existe para eliminar. El redondeo no tiene sesgo.

records.context: **clip, and count.** A gain above 1 at the edge of the microscope field of view can push a near-full-scale pixel past the top of a uint16. Clipping is the only option that keeps the dtype the hook contract requires, and it removes real signal, so every pixel that was *below* full scale before the correction and lands *at* full scale after it is counted and reported. Pixels that were already saturated are not counted: they were saturated at acquisition, not by the correction.

records.source: **clip, and count.** A gain above 1 at the edge of the field can push a near-full-scale pixel past the top of a uint16. Pixels that were already saturated are not counted: they were saturated at acquisition, not by the correction.
records.translation: **recortar, y contar.** Una ganancia superior a 1 en el borde del campo puede llevar un píxel casi a fondo de escala más allá del máximo de un uint16. records.context: A successful illumination correction brings this slope close to zero. The same statistic is used on pixels (the QC images) and on objects (the requirement that the same cell not measure brighter in the middle of the microscope field of view).
records.label: spacr.illumination.position_intensity_slope#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A successful illumination correction brings this slope close to zero. The same statistic is used on pixels (the QC images) and on objects (the requirement that the same cell not measure brighter in the middle of the field).
records.translation: Una corrección de iluminación correcta acerca esta pendiente a cero. El mismo estadístico se usa sobre píxeles (las imágenes de QC) y sobre objetos (el requisito de que la misma célula no se mida más brillante en el centro del campo).

records.context: Intensities are divided by their own mean and the radius is normalised so that 0 is the centre of the microscope field of view and 1 is a corner, so the slope reads as *the fraction of the mean intensity gained or lost between the centre of the microscope field of view and its corner*. -0.30 means a corner object measures 30 % of the mean below a central one.

records.source: Intensities are divided by their own mean and the radius is normalised so that 0 is the centre of the field and 1 is a corner, so the slope reads as *the fraction of the mean intensity gained or lost between the centre of the field and its corner*. -0.30 means a corner object measures 30 % of the mean below a central one.
records.translation: Las intensidades se dividen por su propia media y el radio se normaliza para que 0 sea el centro del campo y 1 una esquina, de modo que la pendiente se lee como *la fracción de la intensidad media que se gana o se pierde entre el centro del campo y su esquina*. -0.30 significa que un objeto de una esquina mide un 30 % de la media por debajo de uno central.

La prueba de solapamiento usa el mismo redondeo que ``compose_window``, de modo que aquí se ofrece una tesela exactamente cuando allí se habría usado; una tesela que no se puede leer se descarta para que el compositor nunca vea un None.

The shipped regex names ``columnID``, ``grna`` and ``rowID``. records.translation: ``src`` debe contener archivos FASTQ comprimidos con gzip cuyos nombres permitan a spaCR emparejar las lecturas R1 y R2.  La ejecución también necesita una tabla de referencia CSV por código de barras, con las columnas ``sequence`` y ``name``.  Una ejecución que decodifica los tres códigos de barras incluidos en spaCR los nombra como ``row_csv``, ``column_csv`` y ``grna_csv``, y una ejecución que decodifica cualquier otro número de códigos de barras los enumera bajo ``barcode_set``, con una entrada por código de barras.  ``target_sequence`` ancla la ventana del código de barras, mientras que ``offset_start``, ``expected_end`` y una expresión regular que nombra un grupo por código de barras describen su disposición.  La expresión regular incluida nombra ``columnID``, ``grna`` y ``rowID``. records.context: Three behaviours can produce plausible but incomplete output.  The anchor match is exact and a wrong regex silently rejects reads; reference sequences are compared in their stored orientation; and a sequence within ``barcode_mismatches`` of two references remains unassigned instead of being guessed.  Separately, read-level HDF5 output can be much larger than the count tables, and high compression may spend more time saving than decoding, so disable ``save_h5`` unless those individual annotations are needed.

records.source: Three behaviours can produce plausible but incomplete output.  The anchor match is exact and a wrong regex silently rejects reads; reference sequences are compared in their stored orientation; and a sequence within ``barcode_mismatches`` of two references remains unassigned instead of being guessed.  Separately, read-level HDF5 output can be much larger than the count tables, and high compression may spend more time saving than decoding, so disable ``save_h5`` unless those individual annotations are needed.
records.translation: Tres comportamientos pueden producir resultados plausibles pero incompletos.  La coincidencia con el ancla es exacta y una expresión regular errónea rechaza lecturas sin avisar; las secuencias de referencia se comparan en la orientación almacenada; y una secuencia que está a ``barcode_mismatches`` o menos de dos referencias queda sin asignar en lugar de adivinarse.  Por otra parte, la salida HDF5 a nivel de lectura puede ser mucho mayor que las tablas de recuentos, y una compresión alta puede dedicar más tiempo a guardar que a decodificar, así que desactive ``save_h5`` salvo que necesite esas anotaciones individuales.

records.translation: Los dos ajustes responden a preguntas distintas. ``target_unique_count`` fija con cuántos gRNAs debería acabar un pocillo y se responde a partir de los recuentos; la calibración busca el corte en el que la imagen y la secuenciación concuerdan y se responde a partir de los pocillos de control. La ejecución informa de ambos números, pero el interruptor solo se lee en ``ml._perform_regression``, por tres motivos.

records.context: Second, in ``ml._perform_regression`` the calibration runs first. When it succeeds ``fraction_threshold`` is no longer ``None``, so this function is not asked for a threshold; the sweep is only drawn, through ``ml._draw_the_threshold_sweep``, which prints the calibrated number beside this sweep's independent pick. If the sweep also read the switch, it would return the calibrated number and both printed values would be the same.

records.context: This module is the analysis that happens **after** :func:`spacr.sequencing.generate_barecode_mapping` has written its ``unique_combinations.csv`` / ``qc.csv``. It answers the two questions a pooled-screen experimenter asks of a mapping run:
records.label: spacr.sequencing_qc#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: This module is the analysis that happens **after** :func:`spacr.sequencing.generate_barecode_mapping` has written its ``unique_combinations.csv`` / ``qc.csv``. It answers the two questions a pooled-screen experimenter asks of a mapping run:
records.translation: Este módulo es el análisis que se hace **después** de que :func:`spacr.sequencing.generate_barecode_mapping` haya escrito sus ``unique_combinations.csv`` / ``qc.csv``. Responde a las dos preguntas que se hace sobre una ejecución de asignación quien experimenta con cribados agrupados:

records.context: 1. *Did the run work?* — reads per microplate sample position and which microplate sample positions are starved, how many reads never mapped, whether the barcode references are distinguishable at all, whether a laboratory microplate row or column is systematically under-read, and how evenly the library is covered. 2. *Where do I cut?* — a gRNA is kept in a microplate sample position when its share of that microplate sample position's reads reaches an abundance threshold. Too low and a microplate sample position collects bleed-through guides it never contained, so no phenotype can be attributed to any one of them; too high and microplate sample positions lose the guides they did contain, and with them the statistical detection sensitivity of the screening experiment.
records.label: spacr.sequencing_qc#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. *Did the run work?* — reads per well and which wells are starved, how many reads never mapped, whether the barcode references are distinguishable at all, whether a plate row or column is systematically under-read, and how evenly the library is covered. 2. *Where do I cut?* — a gRNA is kept in a well when its share of that well's reads reaches an abundance threshold. Too low and a well collects bleed-through guides it never contained, so no phenotype can be attributed to any one of them; too high and wells lose the guides they did contain, and with them the statistical power of the screen.
records.translation: 1. *¿Funcionó la ejecución?* — lecturas por pocillo y qué pocillos tienen muy pocas, cuántas lecturas nunca se asignaron, si las referencias de códigos de barras son siquiera distinguibles, si una fila o columna de la placa recibe sistemáticamente menos lecturas y con qué uniformidad está cubierta la biblioteca. 2. *¿Dónde corto?* — un gRNA se conserva en un pocillo cuando su proporción de las lecturas de ese pocillo alcanza un umbral de abundancia. Demasiado bajo y un pocillo acumula guías contaminantes que nunca contuvo, de modo que no puede atribuirse ningún fenotipo a ninguna de ellas; demasiado alto y los pocillos pierden las guías que sí contenían, y con ellas la potencia estadística del cribado.

records.context: Instead of a hand-picked cutoff (such as 2% of a microplate sample position's reads), the user states the **biological** quantity instead — how many gRNAs per microplate sample position the design intends — and :func:`derive_threshold` solves for the abundance cutoff that delivers it. :func:`threshold_sweep` then walks a range around that cutoff so the trade-off is visible rather than asserted, and :func:`recommend_threshold` writes the answer out in words, with the derived number stated explicitly. The user picks from the curve; nothing here silently picks for them.
records.label: spacr.sequencing_qc#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Instead of a hand-picked cutoff (such as 2% of a well's reads), the user states the **biological** quantity instead — how many gRNAs per well the design intends — and :func:`derive_threshold` solves for the abundance cutoff that delivers it. :func:`threshold_sweep` then walks a range around that cutoff so the trade-off is visible rather than asserted, and :func:`recommend_threshold` writes the answer out in words, with the derived number stated explicitly. The user picks from the curve; nothing here silently picks for them.
records.translation: En lugar de un corte elegido a mano (como el 2% de las lecturas de un pocillo), el usuario indica la magnitud **biológica** — cuántos gRNAs por pocillo pretende el diseño — y :func:`derive_threshold` calcula el corte de abundancia que lo produce. :func:`threshold_sweep` recorre luego un rango en torno a ese corte para que el compromiso sea visible en lugar de afirmarse, y :func:`recommend_threshold` escribe la respuesta en palabras, indicando explícitamente el número derivado. El usuario elige a partir de la curva; nada de aquí elige por él sin avisar.

records.context: **Why a module of its own rather than more of** :mod:`spacr.sequencing`: that module is the read path — FASTQ in, count table out — and it is imported into every ``multiprocessing`` worker of a mapping run. The QC here is a separate, later job over the table that path produced; it pulls in plotting and statistics that the read workers must not pay for, and it is the piece a user re-runs a dozen times while choosing a threshold, long after the reads are mapped.
records.label: spacr.sequencing_qc#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Why a module of its own rather than more of** :mod:`spacr.sequencing`: that module is the read path — FASTQ in, count table out — and it is imported into every ``multiprocessing`` worker of a mapping run. The QC here is a separate, later job over the table that path produced; it pulls in plotting and statistics that the read workers must not pay for, and it is the piece a user re-runs a dozen times while choosing a threshold, long after the reads are mapped.
records.translation: **Por qué un módulo propio y no más de** :mod:`spacr.sequencing`: ese módulo es la ruta de lectura — entra FASTQ, sale una tabla de recuentos — y se importa en cada worker de ``multiprocessing`` de una ejecución de asignación. El QC de aquí es un trabajo independiente y posterior sobre la tabla que produjo esa ruta; incorpora representación gráfica y estadística que los workers de lectura no deben pagar, y es la pieza que un usuario vuelve a ejecutar una docena de veces mientras elige un umbral, mucho después de que las lecturas se hayan asignado.

records.source: See Also: :func:`spacr.sequencing.generate_barecode_mapping` — produces the inputs. :func:`spacr.ml.process_reads` — applies the chosen threshold as ``fraction_threshold`` when the screen is regressed.

records.source: The population is fixed — a well that loses its last gRNA stays in the denominator as a zero — and that is what makes the result a non-increasing function of the threshold: every well's count only ever falls, so every order statistic of them only ever falls. Dropping emptied wells instead would let the median jump *up* when a sparse well is removed, and a target could then be met at two thresholds far apart with no way to say which was meant.
records.translation: La población es fija — un pocillo que pierde su último gRNA permanece en el denominador como un cero —, y eso es lo que hace que el resultado sea una función no creciente del umbral: el recuento de cada pocillo solo puede bajar, así que cualquier estadístico de orden de ellos solo puede bajar. Descartar en cambio los pocillos vaciados permitiría que la mediana *subiera* al eliminar un pocillo escaso, y entonces un objetivo podría alcanzarse con dos umbrales muy distintos sin forma de saber cuál se pretendía.

records.translation: Dos códigos de barras de la misma longitud a ``max_distance`` sustituciones o menos son una **colisión**: una base mal leída traslada una lectura de un pocillo (o de una guía) a otro, y nada posterior puede detectar que ocurrió. También se notifican los duplicados exactos, con distancia 0 — esos son fatales y no solo un riesgo, y :func:`spacr.sequencing.map_sequences_to_names` se niega a ejecutarse con ellos.

records.context: Solve for the abundance threshold that delivers a stated gRNAs-per-microplate sample position target.
records.label: spacr.sequencing_qc.derive_threshold#0
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Solve for the abundance threshold that delivers a stated gRNAs-per-well target.
records.translation: Calcula el umbral de abundancia que produce un objetivo indicado de gRNAs por pocillo.

records.context: The search is exact rather than gridded: the gRNAs-per-microplate sample position statistic is a step function that can only change at a fraction actually present in the table, so every distinct observed fraction is a candidate and the monotonicity of the statistic (see :meth:`WellFractions.statistic_at`) lets a bisection find the answer in ``log2(n)`` evaluations. Where no cutoff hits the target exactly — the statistic is a median of integers and jumps — the candidate landing closest is returned, preferring the one that still *meets* the target over the one that falls short.
records.label: spacr.sequencing_qc.derive_threshold#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The search is exact rather than gridded: the gRNAs-per-well statistic is a step function that can only change at a fraction actually present in the table, so every distinct observed fraction is a candidate and the monotonicity of the statistic (see :meth:`WellFractions.statistic_at`) lets a bisection find the answer in ``log2(n)`` evaluations. Where no cutoff hits the target exactly — the statistic is a median of integers and jumps — the candidate landing closest is returned, preferring the one that still *meets* the target over the one that falls short.
records.translation: La búsqueda es exacta y no en cuadrícula: el estadístico de gRNAs por pocillo es una función escalonada que solo puede cambiar en una fracción realmente presente en la tabla, así que cada fracción observada distinta es una candidata y la monotonía del estadístico (véase :meth:`WellFractions.statistic_at`) permite que una bisección encuentre la respuesta en ``log2(n)`` evaluaciones. Cuando ningún corte alcanza exactamente el objetivo — el estadístico es una mediana de enteros y da saltos —, se devuelve la candidata que queda más cerca, prefiriendo la que todavía *cumple* el objetivo frente a la que se queda corta.

records.context: **The number returned sits in the middle of its plateau, not on its edge.** A whole range of thresholds gives the same gRNAs-per-microplate sample position answer — on a clean run that range is the empty space between the guides a microplate sample position really carried and the bleed-through tail below them, which is exactly what a histogram is being read for when a cutoff is picked by eye. Returning either edge of it would put the cutoff where a re-sequenced run or a rounded count flips guides across it. The geometric middle gives the same answer and is stable; both edges are reported as ``interval_low`` / ``interval_high`` so the width of the plateau — how much slack the choice has — is visible too.
records.label: spacr.sequencing_qc.derive_threshold#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The number returned sits in the middle of its plateau, not on its edge.** A whole range of thresholds gives the same gRNAs-per-well answer — on a clean run that range is the empty space between the guides a well really carried and the bleed-through tail below them, which is exactly what a histogram is being read for when a cutoff is picked by eye. Returning either edge of it would put the cutoff where a re-sequenced run or a rounded count flips guides across it. The geometric middle gives the same answer and is stable; both edges are reported as ``interval_low`` / ``interval_high`` so the width of the plateau — how much slack the choice has — is visible too.
records.translation: **El número devuelto está en el centro de su meseta, no en su borde.** Todo un rango de umbrales da la misma respuesta de gRNAs por pocillo — en una ejecución limpia, ese rango es el espacio vacío entre las guías que realmente contenía un pocillo y la cola de contaminación que queda por debajo, que es exactamente lo que se busca en un histograma cuando se elige un corte a ojo. Devolver cualquiera de los bordes pondría el corte donde una ejecución vuelta a secuenciar o un recuento redondeado hacen que las guías lo crucen. El punto medio geométrico da la misma respuesta y es estable; ambos bordes se indican como ``interval_low`` / ``interval_high``, de modo que también es visible la anchura de la meseta — cuánto margen tiene la elección.

records.label: spacr.spacr_cellpose.cellpose_channel_axis#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``cellpose.transforms.convert_image`` — which ``CellposeModel.eval`` calls with whatever ``channel_axis`` it was handed — indexes ``x.shape[channel_axis]`` and rejects a non-``None`` axis outright for a 2-D input. The two shapes spaCR's loaders produce would therefore both be rejected with a hard-coded ``channel_axis=3``:
records.translation: ``cellpose.transforms.convert_image`` — al que llama ``CellposeModel.eval`` con el ``channel_axis`` que haya recibido — indexa ``x.shape[channel_axis]`` y rechaza directamente un eje distinto de ``None`` para una entrada 2-D. Por tanto, las dos formas que producen los cargadores de spaCR se rechazarían ambas con un ``channel_axis=3`` fijo:

records.context: ``(H, W, C)`` -> ``IndexError: tuple index out of range`` (there is no axis 3 on a 3-D array; the image data channel axis is 2, i.e. ``-1``).

records.translation: Los mapas de activación dicen **dónde** miró un modelo. Esto dice **a qué respondió**, en unidades que un biólogo ya interpreta — área, intensidad, textura —, ajustando un modelo de gradient boosting que reproduce las predicciones del modelo de CV a partir de las características de los objetos que spaCR ya midió, y preguntando después a ese modelo qué usó.

records.context: The two answer different questions and neither replaces the other. A map that lights up the parasite tells you the model attends to the parasite; it does not tell you whether it is responding to the parasite's size, its brightness, or how far it sits from the nucleus.

records.translation: Ambos responden a preguntas distintas y ninguno sustituye al otro. Un mapa que ilumina el parásito indica que el modelo atiende al parásito; no indica si responde a su tamaño, a su brillo o a lo lejos que está del núcleo.

records.source: **Fidelity is reported first.** A surrogate that cannot reproduce the CV model's decisions has explained nothing, and its feature ranking is a ranking of how the features predict each other. So :class:`SurrogateResult` puts it before the importances and :meth:`SurrogateResult.summary` refuses to lead with anything else.
records.translation: **La fidelidad se indica primero.** Un modelo sustituto que no puede reproducir las decisiones del modelo de CV no ha explicado nada, y su clasificación de características es una clasificación de cómo se predicen las características entre sí. Por eso :class:`SurrogateResult` la pone antes de las importancias y :meth:`SurrogateResult.summary` se niega a empezar por otra cosa.

records.source: **The join goes through** ``png_list``. A CV model keys on the crop it scored; the features key on the object. ``png_list`` is the only table that holds both, so it is the bridge — and joining on ``png_path`` alone is not enough, because a path is not stable across machines.
records.translation: **La unión pasa por** ``png_list``. Un modelo de CV se indexa por el recorte que puntuó; las características se indexan por el objeto. ``png_list`` es la única tabla que contiene ambos, así que es el puente — y unir solo por ``png_path`` no basta, porque una ruta no es estable entre máquinas.

records.context: This module holds the two non-xy axes: the **z half** (3D Beta, the first part of the file) and the **t half** built on top of it (4D Beta, the second part, from the ``4D (Beta)`` banner onwards -- it has its own long preamble there). Both are deliberately kept free of Cellpose, of any tracker library and of any model at all, so that the logic can be tested against synthetic label volumes on a CPU in milliseconds: every function here either takes a plain numpy array or takes a ``segment_fn`` callable that the caller supplies. :mod:`spacr.object` provides the Cellpose adapter.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: This module holds the two non-xy axes: the **z half** (3D Beta, the first part of the file) and the **t half** built on top of it (4D Beta, the second part, from the ``4D (Beta)`` banner onwards -- it has its own long preamble there). Both are deliberately kept free of Cellpose, of any tracker library and of any model at all, so that the logic can be tested against synthetic label volumes on a CPU in milliseconds: every function here either takes a plain numpy array or takes a ``segment_fn`` callable that the caller supplies. :mod:`spacr.object` provides the Cellpose adapter.
records.translation: Este módulo contiene los dos ejes que no son xy: la **mitad z** (3D Beta, la primera parte del archivo) y la **mitad t** construida sobre ella (4D Beta, la segunda parte, a partir del encabezado ``4D (Beta)`` -- allí tiene su propio preámbulo extenso). Ambas se mantienen deliberadamente libres de Cellpose, de cualquier biblioteca de seguimiento y de cualquier modelo, para que la lógica pueda probarse con volúmenes de etiquetas sintéticos en una CPU en milisegundos: cada función de aquí toma una matriz de numpy simple o un invocable ``segment_fn`` que proporciona el llamador. :mod:`spacr.object` proporciona el adaptador de Cellpose.

records.context: Scope
records.label: spacr.zstack#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Scope
records.translation: Alcance

records.context: The default ingest route, ``spacr.io._rename_and_organize_image_files``, collapses z before any array reaches segmentation. With ``z_stack=True`` and ``z_segmentation_mode='volumetric'``, :func:`spacr.io.preprocess_img_data` uses a separate raw TIFF route that keeps z, and ``spacr.measure`` accepts ``(Z, Y, X)`` label volumes. :func:`plan_from_settings` returns ``None`` whenever the 3D settings are off -- which is the default -- so the 2-D path is untouched, and :mod:`spacr.object` raises :class:`ZAxisNotPresentError` rather than projecting when the settings are on but the batch it receives has no z axis.
records.label: spacr.zstack#11
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The default ingest route, ``spacr.io._rename_and_organize_image_files``, collapses z before any array reaches segmentation. With ``z_stack=True`` and ``z_segmentation_mode='volumetric'``, :func:`spacr.io.preprocess_img_data` uses a separate raw TIFF route that keeps z, and ``spacr.measure`` accepts ``(Z, Y, X)`` label volumes. :func:`plan_from_settings` returns ``None`` whenever the 3D settings are off -- which is the default -- so the 2-D path is untouched, and :mod:`spacr.object` raises :class:`ZAxisNotPresentError` rather than projecting when the settings are on but the batch it receives has no z axis.
records.translation: La ruta de ingesta predeterminada, ``spacr.io._rename_and_organize_image_files``, colapsa z antes de que ninguna matriz llegue a la segmentación. Con ``z_stack=True`` y ``z_segmentation_mode='volumetric'``, :func:`spacr.io.preprocess_img_data` usa una ruta TIFF sin procesar aparte que conserva z, y ``spacr.measure`` acepta volúmenes de etiquetas ``(Z, Y, X)``. :func:`plan_from_settings` devuelve ``None`` siempre que los ajustes 3D están desactivados -- que es el valor predeterminado --, de modo que la ruta 2-D no se toca, y :mod:`spacr.object` lanza :class:`ZAxisNotPresentError` en lugar de proyectar cuando los ajustes están activados pero el lote que recibe no tiene eje z.

records.context: The two halves live in one file rather than two because a 4-D acquisition is a z-stack per timepoint and the t code delegates to the z code for every one of them -- ``segment_4d`` is a loop around :func:`segment_3d`, ``track_4d``'s overlap backend *is* :func:`stitch_planes` applied along t, and ``TStackSpec`` carries a :class:`ZStackSpec` inside it. Nothing in the z half below knows the t half exists, so a 3-D run is unaffected by any of it.
records.label: spacr.zstack#2

records.source: The two halves live in one file rather than two because a 4-D acquisition is a z-stack per timepoint and the t code delegates to the z code for every one of them -- ``segment_4d`` is a loop around :func:`segment_3d`, ``track_4d``'s overlap backend *is* :func:`stitch_planes` applied along t, and ``TStackSpec`` carries a :class:`ZStackSpec` inside it. records.context: Four things drive the design of the z half, and each of them is a place where a naive 3-D implementation silently produces wrong science:

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Four things drive the design of the z half, and each of them is a place where a naive 3-D implementation silently produces wrong science:
records.translation: Cuatro cosas determinan el diseño de la mitad z, y cada una de ellas es un punto en el que una implementación 3-D ingenua produce sin aviso ciencia errónea:

records.context: **Anisotropy must be known.** Confocal z-spacing is routinely 3-10x the xy pixel size. A volume segmented as if it were isotropic merges objects along z, because a 3-image-layer gap that is really 3 um reads to the segmenter as 3 pixels. ``anisotropy`` here always means ``dz / dxy`` -- the z step divided by the xy pixel size -- which is the same convention Cellpose uses. It is a *required* input for volumetric segmentation: :func:`resolve_anisotropy` raises :class:`UnknownAnisotropyError` rather than defaulting to 1.0, because 1.0 is a claim about the microscope, not a neutral value.
records.label: spacr.zstack#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Anisotropy must be known.** Confocal z-spacing is routinely 3-10x the xy pixel size. A volume segmented as if it were isotropic merges objects along z, because a 3-plane gap that is really 3 um reads to the segmenter as 3 pixels. ``anisotropy`` here always means ``dz / dxy`` -- the z step divided by the xy pixel size -- which is the same convention Cellpose uses. It is a *required* input for volumetric segmentation: :func:`resolve_anisotropy` raises :class:`UnknownAnisotropyError` rather than defaulting to 1.0, because 1.0 is a claim about the microscope, not a neutral value.
records.translation: **Hay que conocer la anisotropía.** El espaciado en z del confocal suele ser 3-10x el tamaño de píxel en xy. Un volumen segmentado como si fuera isótropo fusiona objetos a lo largo de z, porque un hueco de 3 planos que en realidad mide 3 um le parece al segmentador de 3 píxeles. Aquí ``anisotropy`` significa siempre ``dz / dxy`` -- el paso en z dividido por el tamaño de píxel en xy --, que es la misma convención que usa Cellpose. Es una entrada *obligatoria* para la segmentación volumétrica: :func:`resolve_anisotropy` lanza :class:`UnknownAnisotropyError` en lugar de usar 1.0 por defecto, porque 1.0 es una afirmación sobre el microscopio, no un valor neutro.

records.context: **Stitching 2-D image layers is not 3-D segmentation.** Both are legitimate and they give different answers. Per-image-layer segmentation followed by IoU linking (:data:`MODE_STITCH`) sees each image layer independently and cannot recover an object that is invisible in one image layer; true volumetric segmentation (:data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC`) uses the z gradient but is far more sensitive to a wrong anisotropy. The mode is therefore explicit, never inferred, and :class:`ZStackResult` records which one actually ran so it can be written next to the numbers it produced.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Stitching 2-D planes is not 3-D segmentation.** Both are legitimate and they give different answers. Per-plane segmentation followed by IoU linking (:data:`MODE_STITCH`) sees each plane independently and cannot recover an object that is invisible in one plane; true volumetric segmentation (:data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC`) uses the z gradient but is far more sensitive to a wrong anisotropy. The mode is therefore explicit, never inferred, and :class:`ZStackResult` records which one actually ran so it can be written next to the numbers it produced.
records.translation: **Unir planos 2-D no es segmentación 3-D.** Ambas son legítimas y dan respuestas distintas. La segmentación por planos seguida del enlace por IoU (:data:`MODE_STITCH`) ve cada plano por separado y no puede recuperar un objeto que es invisible en un plano; la verdadera segmentación volumétrica (:data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC`) usa el gradiente en z, pero es mucho más sensible a una anisotropía errónea. Por eso el modo es explícito, nunca se deduce, y :class:`ZStackResult` registra cuál se ejecutó realmente para que pueda escribirse junto a los números que produjo.

records.context: **Objects touching the first or last image layer are truncated.** Exactly as an object touching the xy microscope field of view edge is truncated. Their volume is a lower bound and their shape statistics are meaningless. :func:`flag_truncated_z` marks them, mirroring the reasoning ``spacr.seg_qc`` already established for xy border objects (see ``seg_qc._score_labels``, which counts border objects and then excludes them from every size statistic).

records.context: A z-stack is ``n_z`` times a microscope field of view, and volumetric segmentation transiently needs several copies of it. :func:`estimate_peak_bytes` gives the number for a given microscope field of view; the workflow processes **one microscope field of view at a time** and never holds a laboratory microplate. For a 2048x2048 microscope field of view at 21 image layers in float32 that is ~350 MB for the volume, and ~1.4 GB peak in :data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC` with resampling at anisotropy 5 (the isotropic copy is ``anisotropy`` times taller). records.source: A z-stack is ``n_z`` times a field, and volumetric segmentation transiently needs several copies of it. :func:`estimate_peak_bytes` gives the number for a given field; the pipeline processes **one field at a time** and never holds a plate. For a 2048x2048 field at 21 planes in float32 that is ~350 MB for the volume, and ~1.4 GB peak in :data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC` with resampling at anisotropy 5 (the isotropic copy is ``anisotropy`` times taller). records.translation: Una pila z es ``n_z`` veces un campo, y la segmentación volumétrica necesita temporalmente varias copias de ella. :func:`estimate_peak_bytes` da la cifra para un campo dado; el pipeline procesa **un campo cada vez** y nunca mantiene una placa entera. Para un campo de 2048x2048 con 21 planos en float32, son ~350 MB para el volumen y un pico de ~1.4 GB en :data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC` con remuestreo a anisotropía 5 (la copia isótropa es ``anisotropy`` veces más alta). records.context: Each image layer is compared with the image layer below it, and the pairing is greedy and **one-to-one**: pairs are considered in descending IoU and a label may take part in at most one link. That is what stops two genuinely different objects that merely happen to overlap the same object in xy from being fused -- only the better match inherits the label, the other starts a new one. Any pair below ``iou_threshold`` is not linked at all.
records.label: spacr.zstack.stitch_planes#1

records.source: Each plane is compared with the plane below it, and the pairing is greedy and **one-to-one**: pairs are considered in descending IoU and a label may take part in at most one link. That is what stops two genuinely different objects that merely happen to overlap the same object in xy from being fused -- only the better match inherits the label, the other starts a new one. Any pair below ``iou_threshold`` is not linked at all.
records.translation: Cada plano se compara con el plano inferior, y el emparejamiento es voraz y **uno a uno**: los pares se consideran por IoU descendente y una etiqueta puede participar como mucho en un enlace. Eso es lo que impide que se fusionen dos objetos realmente distintos que simplemente se solapan con el mismo objeto en xy -- solo el mejor emparejamiento hereda la etiqueta, y el otro empieza una nueva. Ningún par por debajo de ``iou_threshold`` se enlaza.

records.source: Unlike ``cellpose.utils.stitch3D``, new labels are always drawn from a single monotonically increasing counter. records.translation: A diferencia de ``cellpose.utils.stitch3D``, las etiquetas nuevas siempre se toman de un único contador monótonamente creciente. records.context: Every column's unit is in :data:`VOLUME_STATS_UNITS`, and the names carry the unit too, because a 3-D run produces *voxel counts* where a 2-D run produces px^2 areas. Writing one into a column named for the other is the single easiest way to silently corrupt a screen.

records.source: Every column's unit is in :data:`VOLUME_STATS_UNITS`, and the names carry the unit too, because a 3-D run produces *voxel counts* where a 2-D run produces px^2 areas. Writing one into a column named for the other is the single easiest way to silently corrupt a screen.
records.translation: La unidad de cada columna está en :data:`VOLUME_STATS_UNITS`, y los nombres también llevan la unidad, porque una ejecución 3-D produce *recuentos de vóxeles* donde una 2-D produce áreas en px^2. Escribir unos en una columna con el nombre de las otras es la forma más fácil de corromper un cribado sin que nadie lo note.

records.context: With anisotropic voxels the physical numbers differ from the voxel counts by more than a constant: the surface area weights each face by the area of the face, so a z-facing face (``dy*dx``) and an x-facing face (``dz*dy``) contribute differently. Passing ``voxel_size=None`` gives the voxel-count columns only.
records.label: spacr.zstack.volume_stats#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: With anisotropic voxels the physical numbers differ from the voxel counts by more than a constant: the surface area weights each face by the area of the face, so a z-facing face (``dy*dx``) and an x-facing face (``dz*dy``) contribute differently. Passing ``voxel_size=None`` gives the voxel-count columns only.
records.translation: Con vóxeles anisótropos, los números físicos difieren de los recuentos de vóxeles en algo más que una constante: el área de la superficie pondera cada cara por su área, de modo que una cara orientada en z (``dy*dx``) y una orientada en x (``dz*dy``) contribuyen de forma distinta. Pasar ``voxel_size=None`` da solo las columnas de recuento de vóxeles.

records.source: Size is reported in exactly one column, never two: ``volume_voxels`` for a ``(T, Z, Y, X)`` stack and ``area_px2`` for a ``(T, Y, X)`` one. They are different quantities and writing one into the other's column is the single easiest way to corrupt a screen -- the same point :data:`spacr.zstack.VOLUME_STATS_UNITS` exists to make. Micrometre and second columns appear only when the voxel size and frame interval are known.
records.translation: El tamaño se indica exactamente en una columna, nunca en dos: ``volume_voxels`` para una pila ``(T, Z, Y, X)`` y ``area_px2`` para una ``(T, Y, X)``. Son magnitudes distintas, y escribir una en la columna de la otra es la forma más fácil de corromper un cribado -- la misma idea que :data:`spacr.zstack.VOLUME_STATS_UNITS` existe para transmitir. Las columnas en micrómetros y en segundos solo aparecen cuando se conocen el tamaño de vóxel y el intervalo entre fotogramas.
